task_name: The hooks in the checkout's local settings, purged before they are written

rubric.result: The objective promises two things: installing the hooks removes the app's own stale entries for every event it is about to write, and leaves every foreign hook exactly where it was. Both are produced by production lines. `install` loops over `EVENTS` ('UserPromptSubmit', 'Notification', 'Stop') and sets `hooks[event] = [...#purged(hooks[event]), #ownGroup()]`; `#purged` drops every entry whose `command` contains `MARKER` and drops a group left with no hooks, keeping the rest of each group by `{...group, hooks}` — so a foreign group keeps its own keys (a `matcher`, as `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` shows a real one carries) and its position, ours being appended after it. `{...settings, hooks}` and `{...existing}` keep every top-level setting and every event the adapter does not write. One edge remains outside both promises: `#withoutOwnEntries` returns `null` for a group that is not an object, so a non-object element of an event array would be dropped rather than left where it was; that shape is not a valid Claude Code settings file and the contract says nothing about it, so I record it here rather than as a finding.

The **TDD:** line asks for `it('purges its own stale hooks for every event before writing the new ones')` with an arrange holding one of ours pointing at a dead port under `Stop` plus a foreign `Stop` hook, and the assertion that the written JSON has exactly one of ours under `Stop` and still holds the foreign one. The test at line 88 of the new test file arranges exactly that: `read` answers `{hooks: {Stop: [STALE_OWN_GROUP, FOREIGN_STOP_GROUP]}}`, where `STALE_OWN_GROUP` carries the `CT_SESSION_HOOKS_URL` guard but posts to `http://localhost:4009/hooks` (the dead port) and `FOREIGN_STOP_GROUP` is `echo goodbye`. The assertion is `expect(write).toHaveBeenCalledWith(SETTINGS_PATH, ...)` against the whole literal document, whose `Stop` is `[FOREIGN_STOP_GROUP, OWN_GROUP]` — one of ours, the foreign one still there and in its place. Same input, same expected value, stricter than the sentence rather than weaker.

The `Contract (backend/src/infrastructure/local-settings-session-hooks.ts)` block is matched symbol by symbol: `export class LocalSettingsSessionHooks extends SessionHooks`, `SETTINGS = ['.claude', 'settings.local.json']`, `EVENTS = ['UserPromptSubmit', 'Notification', 'Stop']`, `MARKER = 'CT_SESSION_HOOKS_URL'`, `TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5`, and `COMMAND` character for character including the mixed quoting of `--data-binary @- \"$CT_SESSION_HOOKS_URL\"`; the constructor destructures `{ read, write }` with the two declared function types. The prose of the block holds too: one group `{hooks: [{type: 'command', command: COMMAND, timeout: TIMEOUT_SECONDS}]}` per event (`#ownGroup`), an entry is ours when its `command` contains `MARKER` (`#isOwnEntry`), a group left with no hooks is dropped (`hooks.length === 0 ? null : ...`), a missing file is an empty object (`if (text === null) return {}`), a non-JSON file raises `SessionHooksNotUnderstood` before any write, a failing write raises `SessionHooksNotWritten` — both are the existing domain exceptions under `SessionHooksFailure`, unchanged by this diff. The one clause with no code behind it is 'an event left with no groups loses its key': within the contract's own scope — the three events, each of which always gets ours appended — that state cannot occur, and `conventions/simplicity.md` ('An unreachable check is not a check') forbids writing the branch, so its absence is right rather than a deviation.

Row by row: D-10 (everything new under `backend/` is TypeScript) — both new files are `.ts` and `npm run typecheck` is green. D-16 (no new module under `backend/src` names cmux) — neither file mentions cmux. D-11 (a yardstick is imported from the plugin, never reimplemented) — the plugin implements nothing that writes hooks into a governed checkout's `.claude/settings.local.json`; `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` is the plugin's own manifest, a different thing, so nothing is reimplemented here. D-25 (the backend hands over paths and pastes no text into a prompt) — this diff writes a hook command, not a prompt, and the hook posts its payload with `--data-binary @-` rather than carrying text in an argument. D-22 (the gates are the human's) — no endpoint or trigger is added. D-1, D-13, D-18, D-21, D-26 and the entrance button's literal are about the cabin, the phase and the front, and no line of this diff bears on them. No row is implemented with a value other than the one it states.

Exemplars: §3 names `backend/src/infrastructure/disk-implementation-start-registry.ts` and the adapter plays the same role and matches its idiom closely — injected `read`/`write` function types declared at module level, static constants, a `#isRecord` type guard, `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)` plus a trailing newline as the written payload; the new test file mirrors `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/disk-implementation-start-registry.test.ts` (module-level literal fixtures, `vi.fn()` sinks, an assertion on `toHaveBeenCalledWith(path, literal)`), so the house idiom for this kind of adapter is matched, not invented. Rules: I read `CLAUDE.md` (English identifiers, test names and diagnostics — satisfied; nothing here renders to a person, so the Spanish exemption has no subject), `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` (TypeScript-only and erasable syntax, the `infrastructure/` layout, the two-cause exception family `*NotWritten`/`*NotUnderstood` — all satisfied) and `.agent/conventions-ack.md` (about claim/dispatch-check, no subject here). `frontend/README.md` has no subject. I loaded `backend-engineering:backend-best-practices`: it is a router for Python Django/FastAPI references and explicitly yields to the project's conventions, which `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` restates as precedence item 3; nothing in it bears on this diff beyond what the yardstick already says. ct's yardstick: `architecture.md` — an adapter in `infrastructure/`, one concept per module, extending the domain port, no import upward; `boundaries.md` — the adapter is named after its implementation and not after its port, the foreign format is handled by projection (rejecting unknown keys would break every real settings file, and preserving them is what the objective requires), there is no cast in production code, and the parse failure is translated into a domain exception before leaving the layer; `domain.md` — the tool's nouns (`.claude`, `settings.local.json`, the event names) stay inside `infrastructure/`, as this repository requires; `simplicity.md` — the only guard on shape sits at the door the foreign file arrives through, and the class's one public method is the port's, wired by a later task of this same plan (line ~700 of the plan file). `defects.md`, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — the three event names are Claude Code's own contract data, iterated rather than dispatched over, with no hand comparison and no catch-all branch, so the rule has no subject here; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — the closest call in the diff: `#purged`, `#withoutOwnEntries` and `#ownGroup` pass `JsonRecord`s between private methods, but the map *is* the foreign JSON document at the serialization boundary, never leaves the module and never becomes a domain answer, which is the same position the named exemplar's `static recordFor(): Record<string, unknown>` occupies, so I do not read this as the defect; (3) two fields that have to agree / a sentinel — none; the absence of the file is carried in the type as `Promise<string | null>`, which is what the rule asks for, not the empty string; (4) an error named for where it happens — `SessionHooksNotUnderstood` and `SessionHooksNotWritten` are named for what happened, hang off `SessionHooksFailure`, and are raised at the right causes. Two tensions I declare rather than report: the env-var name `CT_SESSION_HOOKS_URL` now lives as a literal in two modules (`ClaudeConversations.HOOKS_URL_VARIABLE` from task 4 and `MARKER`/`COMMAND` here) with no test comparing the two halves, which `conventions/decisions.md` names as an antipattern — but both literals are prescribed verbatim by the plan's Contract blocks that item 3 measures, so the implementer could not have written it otherwise; and `boundaries.md`'s 'the adapter does not choose the cap' reads against the plan's `static readonly TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5`, though the cap here is written into a config file for Claude Code to apply rather than applied to a call this adapter makes.

The diff has no `-` lines at all: both files are `new file mode 100644`, 214 insertions and 0 deletions, and no pre-existing test file is touched. There is no assertion, case or test that ended up asserting less.

The promised behaviour lives in `backend/src/infrastructure/local-settings-session-hooks.ts`: the purge is `#isOwnEntry` matching `MARKER` inside `#withoutOwnEntries`/`#purged`, the append is the `for (const event of EVENTS)` loop, the preservation is the `{...group, hooks}` and `{...settings, hooks}` spreads. The test's own scaffolding is only the two `vi.fn()` sinks and the literal settings fixtures; the assertions are on the document the production code handed to `write`, not on a stub's return value or on a count of calls standing in for an effect. Revert the production file and the tests cannot even import it, let alone pass.

`**Files:**` declares the adapter and its test, both `(create)`, and the diff writes those two files and nothing else — no plan hunk, so there is no amendment to rule on. Inside them, every line traces to a sentence of the task: the constants and the constructor to the Contract block, the purge loop to the Objective, the six tests to the `**Tests:**` list name for name, and the absence of any `SessionStart` hook to the third **Verification:** command and the note beside it. Nothing named in `### Out of scope` is touched: no `POST /start-plan` file, no `PlanCollapse` row, no gate, no groom, no dispatcher, no `Home`. No refactor of neighbouring modules, no extra helper, no adjacent fix.

Six new tests, all in the file this task creates. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no network, no filesystem, no randomness and no sleep — `read` and `write` are `vi.fn()` doubles and every expected value is a literal built in the file. Isolated: each test constructs its own doubles and its own adapter inside its body, there is no shared mutable state, no fixed path on disk, no port, and no order dependency between them — the module-level constants are frozen-by-use literals that no test writes to. Verifies real behaviour: five assert on the document the production code passed to `write` (the observable effect) and one on the exception type the production code raises, plus `expect(write).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` proving the unparseable file is not overwritten; none asserts a mock's call count as a stand-in for an effect. I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` and its `testing-anti-patterns.md` reference for the finer half and found nothing in this file that contradicts a sentence of either: the doubles are the injected `read`/`write` seam rather than mocks of the unit under test, the mock setup is three lines against longer assertions, each name states one behaviour, and the settings fixture mirrors a real hook group shape (`plugin/hooks/hooks.json` shows a group without a `matcher` is real). One observation kept out of findings, since it is not one of the three and I can pin it to no sentence of that skill: `leaves hooks that are not ours exactly where they were` asserts with `toContainEqual`, which would not notice a change of position — but the first test in the same file pins the whole written document, `Stop` included, in order.
